t: "Python Performance Matters" by Emery Berger (Strange Loop 2022)
desc: It's 2022. Moore's Law and Dennard scaling have run out of steam, making it harder than ever to achieve high performance - especially in Python. This talk first explains in detail the unique challenges that Python poses to programmers. It then presents Scalene, a novel high-performance CPU, GPU and memory profiler for Python that does many things that past Python profilers do not and cannot do. Sc

recs.stt: Buffers on the Edge: Python and Rust
recs.x:
All I took away was the age-old adage of: try to avoid passing objects back and forth from native code and also that I write inefficient code that copies buffers more often than I thought.

If you’re interested in python performance I saw a really good talk from strangeloop this year titled "Python Performance Matters": [link] ; Emery Berger has been talking about python performance for quite some time.

recs.stt: I/O is no longer the bottleneck
recs.x:
Emery Berger has a great talk [1] where he argues that it is mostly pointless to optimize python code, if your program is slow, you should look for a properly optimized library to do that work for you.
